findings.location: section 6, paragraph 'What survives and what cancels, in words' (line 377; same sentence in the .tex at line 476)
findings.problem: The document says that for dirac16complex00 the term 3H gamma^(x8) is 'a term of the field equation that no frame or coordinate choice removes'. This is false. The value gamma^mu Omega_mu = 3H gamma^(x8) belongs to the diagonal vielbein. Another admissible vielbein of the same metric, with its own canonical spin connection, makes gamma^mu Omega_mu vanish identically for every H > 0 and every a4. What the record does prove is narrower: Omega_mu itself cannot vanish in any frame, because its curvature is the Riemann tensor. No Revision check supports the stronger claim.
findings.evidence: Independent sympy computation (scratch boost2.py, about 60 s). Start from the diagonal vielbein e^a_mu = f_a delta^a_mu and boost the frame in the (x4, x8) plane: e'^(4) = cosh(b) e^(4) + sinh(b) e^(8), e'^(8) = sinh(b) e^(4) + cosh(b) e^(8), with rapidity b = 6 H x4 + c0. Results: the metric is unchanged; omega' is antisymmetric; the vielbein postulate holds for all components; Omega'_mu is nonzero for mu = x1..x7; and gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = 0 exactly, with a4(x4) symbolic and H > 0. The hand derivation agrees: gamma^mu Omega_mu = (1/2) div(e_b) gamma^b + (1/4) omega_[cab] gamma^cab. The boost makes every frame divergence vanish, and the totally antisymmetric part stays zero. The same term is also removed within the diagonal frame by the field rescaling Phi = sin^(-1/2)(z) chi. The document's own exact family shows this: alpha = -1/2 gives M = -m gamma^(x4), with no H term.
findings.fix: Delete the clause 'that no frame or coordinate choice removes'. State instead: gamma^mu Omega_mu = 3H gamma^(x8) is the value for the diagonal vielbein, and it vanishes in, for example, the frame boosted in the (x4, x8) plane with rapidity 6 H x4. What cannot be removed in any frame is Omega_mu itself (curvature R^(x8)_(x8) = -6H^2), together with the frame factors. Add this frame dependence to section 15 ('What is not claimed').

findings.location: section 15, third bullet (line 539)
findings.problem: The document says 'In flat 4+4 space every energy eigenspace of the one-particle generator has Krein inertia (4,4)'. As a general statement this is false. Eigenspaces of the growing extra-time modes, which have complex energy and are discussed in section 11 of the same document, are Krein-neutral: B restricted to them is zero. The cited checks verify only finite samples with real energy: six samples on the Wolfram side and one (m=1, k1=2, k8=2) on the sympy side.
findings.evidence: Independent sympy computation (scratch krein_complex.py) with the Revision gammas and h_m(k) = -i m gamma^(x4) - gamma^(x4) sum k_a gamma^a. For m = 1, k5 = 2 (the document's own example, E = +-i sqrt3), the eigenspaces have dimension 8 and u^dagger B v restricted to them has eigenvalues {0: 8}. The same holds for m = 1, k = (1,0,0,0,2,0,0,0). For a real-energy case with extra-time momentum (m = 2, k5 = 1), the inertia is (4,4). The general reason: B h = h^dagger B gives (E - conj E) u^dagger B u = 0.
findings.fix: Restrict the statement to real energies: every real-energy eigenspace has Krein inertia (4,4), and complex-energy eigenspaces are Krein-neutral. Or say 'at the computed samples', as PAIR_CREATION_PROOFS section 11.2 item 8 already does.

The theorems prove an invertible map between the solution sets of two parameter sets. They do not prove that universes come in pairs. Section 11.2 item 3 of the same document says that 'a single universe with mass +m is an equally valid solution without its partner'. findings.evidence: Line 623: 'Proved: universes of masses $+m$ and $-m$ come in pairs in the precise sense of the theorems T1 and T2.'
